results.title: Chocolate Pelamushi: Georgian cornmeal dessert prepared with whole milk and dark chocolate
results.description: Chocolate Milk Pelamushi is a dense, silky dessert that adapts the traditional Georgian cornmeal base into a velvet-like cream. By utilizing 3.2% fat milk as the primary liquid, the result shifts from the translucent nature of grape-based versions to a structured, creamy consistency capable of holding its shape after chilling. The Primacy of the Flour Paste The structural integrity of the dessert depends entirely on the initial emulsion. Combining 70 g of fine cornmeal and 20 g of high-grade wheat flour with a small portion of the total 600 ml of cold milk is the most critical stage of the process. The cook must ensure this paste is a perfectly homogeneous liquid, devoid of any dry clumps. This specific preparation is the only way to guarantee a smooth thickening process; introducing dry flour directly into hot liquid would inevitably result in lumps, compromising the silkiness of the final texture. Thermal Control and Thickening The remaining milk is heated with 80 g of granulated sugar, 1 tsp of vanilla sugar, and a pinch of salt. The liquid must reach the threshold of boiling-ensuring all sugar crystals are dissolved-before the heat is reduced to a minimum. The flour paste is then introduced in a thin stream while whisking intensely.
